column1: # RENAME_SCOPE.tsv — what a public-procedure rename touches, and what it does not
# Ian Howell — Embodied Music Lab — GPL-3.0-or-later
# THE SCOPE IS A FILE, NOT A FLAG IN FOUR SCRIPTS. Before this file existed the
# same exemption set was restated in list_sites.sh, in v159's section A, in the
# grep that built the rename inventory, and in the work order — and they
# disagreed. The inventory's grep searched four extensions and missed sixteen
# shell scripts, one of which passes a procedure name as a live argument. The
# reconciliation the ruling ordered before editing is what caught it.
# RULING_RENAME_SCOPE_2026-09-02.md settles the scope by KIND and orders it
# stated once, here, for every consumer to read.
# THREE COLUMNS, TAB SEPARATED:
#   pattern      A path fragment. A row matches a file when the fragment
#                appears anywhere in its repository-relative path. No globs —
#                a pattern that can match a file nobody has written yet is not
#                a statement about what exists.
#   disposition  RENAME | REGENERATE | UNTOUCHED | OUT_OF_SCOPE
#   why          one line, for the reader deciding whether the row is right.
# THE DISPOSITIONS, from the ruling:
#   RENAME       Live code and live hand-maintained inputs. A retired name here
#                is a silent-until-run failure. The default for anything not
#                matched by a row below.
#   REGENERATE   Has a committed generator. Run the generator after the rename
#                and byte-compare. Hand-editing a generated file is the defect
#                the drift checks exist to catch, whatever the reason.
#   UNTOUCHED    The output of a past run. It records what the old code produced
#                under its old names. It cannot be regenerated until the
#                authoritative run, and editing it would falsify a record.
#   OUT_OF_SCOPE Narrative and dated records. A record of what was true when
#                written keeps its words — the mailbox principle, extended.
# ANYTHING NOT MATCHED HERE IS RENAME. That default is deliberate: a new file
# nobody thought about is live code until someone says otherwise, and the cost
# of a needless rename is smaller than the cost of a missed one.
pattern
column3: why

column1: .git/
column3: Git's own storage. Not source.

column1: mailbox/
column3: Correspondence. A note is never edited once written; the newest file on a topic supersedes rather than revises.

column1: _mailbox_live/
column3: The live mailbox. Same rule as the archive.

column1: audit/
column3: Dated audit records. What was true when written.

column1: handoff/
column3: Session handoff packets, dated. Same rule.

column1: docs/error-census/
column3: A census report of what the tree held at a date, not a declaration the code reads.

column1: docs/frozen-choice-map/
column3: A correspondence map recorded at a date.

column1: planning/
column3: Planning registers and trackers, dated.

column1: /out/
column3: Harness run output. Produced by that harness's own run.sh.

column1: /replay_out/
column3: Recorder replay output. Same.

column1: /stress_out/
column3: Stress-harness output. Same.

column1: /qq_out/
column3: Q-Q harness output. Same.

column1: __pycache__/
column3: Python bytecode. Rebuilt on import.

column1: walkthrough/kit/coverage_map.tsv
column3: Emitted by walkthrough/kit/build_coverage_map.py.

column1: walkthrough/kit/table_s2.tsv
column3: Emitted by walkthrough/kit/build_table_s2.py.

column1: walkthrough/kit/results/
column3: Output of a past kit run. Superseded by the authoritative run, not repaired.

column1: walkthrough/kit/audit/
column3: Per-run evidence tables. Same.

column1: walkthrough/kit/audit/rename_call_sites.tsv
column3: The rename inventory itself. It lists the retired names by definition, and searching it would make the census include itself and never settle.

column1: walkthrough/kit/build_rename_inventory.sh
column3: The inventory generator. Its old-to-new mapping table states the rename; renaming the left-hand side would erase the mapping it exists to record.

column1: RENAME_SCOPE.tsv
column3: This file. It describes the rename and is not a caller of anything.
